statement: A participant release caller whose original bounded deadline expires while awaiting a delivered reply cannot treat that reply's CUT_OVER, OBSERVED or other positive outcome as current permission. The one canonical participant-release-client response boundary must fail closed based on the same original TimeSource, without cancelling durable effects or inventing a new transport driver.

constraints.statement: Only existing src/node/participant-release-client.js owns caller deadline classification after await. Reuse its original timeSource and release contract; do not modify Raft, replica receipt, transit transport, membership, admission, origin, session clocks or add a second delayed callback.

After an original non-OBSERVE request's successful transport delivery, check that original caller deadline is still unspent before interpreting positive answer or redirect. A late positive becomes typed UNAVAILABLE with missingFact RELEASE_DEADLINE; never report an already-committed action as rolled back. Existing partition/recovery owners reconstruct durable outcome instead of treating late reply as authorization.

The existing original request validation, before-send timeout, transport classification, and OBSERVE_APPLIED_POSITION's independently owned observation deadline remain unchanged. Unavailable/invalid reply precedence and malformed deadline handling must preserve existing behavior; prevent NOT_LEADER redirect if the first reply arrives after deadline.

Use a deterministic TimeSource with an actual accepted and classified original delivery response: clock advances beyond the same request.deadlineAtMs strictly while awaiting. Original caller currently reports CUT_OVER: named source-only negative must engage its actual client route rather than a fake outcome checker, trivial zero budget, timer cancellation or virtual worker simulation.

Use a controlled test with before/at/after boundary, no positive may cross expiry; no extra delivery or timeout scheduled and same one original clock; preserve earlier healthy completion. A delivered operation after expiry may still be durable and cannot be uncommitted; failure must retain recovery responsibility.

Retain original 20s release / 1s election benchmark separation and lossless test evidence, unchanged native V10, release protocol, recovery, TX1/TX2, FreshMG, off-seed, CDC and zero-legacy checks; independent current-source review and locked-host 3/5-node gates before any merge/main or receipt completion.
